transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic, can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling extremely depressed and empty for about a month now. I also feel constantly anxious because I feel like people are watching or monitoring me all the time. It has just become really hard to handle.
Can you tell me more about feeling like people are watching or monitoring you, is this something you believe is actually happening or does it just feel that way to you?

It is definitely happening, they are absolutely monitoring me and keeping track of what I do. It's not just a vague feeling, and the constant surveillance is making me feel incredibly anxious and unsafe every single day. I can't find any peace because of it.
For how long have you been experiencing these depressive symptoms, and have they been present throughout the time you've believed you're being monitored, or did they start after the monitoring began?

The depressive feelings have been really bad for about a month now, but the monitoring has been going on for much longer, for about eight months. So the feeling of being watched started long before this heavy depression set in, though now I'm dealing with both at the same time.
Have you experienced any hearing or seeing things that others cannot, or any other unusual perceptions, aside from the feeling of being monitored?

Yes, I've been hearing whispers when no one is around, and sometimes I see shadowy figures out of the corner of my eye. This has been happening for a long time now, even during the months before I started feeling so depressed. It's really unsettling because they feel so real.

Can you estimate how much of the past eight months, when you've believed you're being monitored and experienced these other perceptions, have been dominated by depressive symptoms versus periods where you didn't feel depressed but still had the delusions and hallucinations?

Actually, these issues have been going on for over a year now, about a year and four months in total. Throughout most of that entire time, I've been struggling with these heavy feelings of depression. There were only a few brief weeks here and there where I didn't feel depressed, but the monitoring and the whispers were still happening.

Would you say that the depressive symptoms have been a major part of your experience for most of the time you've been having these delusions and hallucinations, or have the delusions and hallucinations been the dominant symptoms?

The depression has definitely been there for the vast majority of the time, making up most of the last year and four months. Even though the monitoring and whispers have been constant, the heavy sadness and emptiness have been dragging me down almost the entire time. There were only very short periods where I wasn't depressed but still experienced those other things.

Can you clarify if there has been a period of at least two weeks where you experienced delusions and hallucinations without any significant depressive symptoms, or have the depressive symptoms always been present when you've had these psychotic experiences?

Yes, there have been times like that. There was a period of about three weeks earlier this year where my mood felt completely normal, but I was still hearing the whispers and felt certain I was being monitored. So those experiences definitely happened even when I wasn't feeling depressed at all.

During that three-week period when your mood was normal but you still had the delusions and hallucinations, did those psychotic symptoms dominate your experience, or were they relatively manageable and not the main focus of your daily life?

Even though my mood was okay during those three weeks, the whispers and the feeling of being monitored were still very intense and dominated everything. It was still incredibly hard to function or focus on daily life because those experiences were so active and overwhelming.
Do you think the depressive symptoms or the delusions and hallucinations have been the primary issue for you overall, considering the entire duration of your experiences?

Both have been incredibly challenging to deal with, but the depression has felt like it has been there for the majority of the overall time. However, there were also times, lasting at least a couple of weeks, when the delusions and hallucinations were happening even when I wasn't feeling deeply depressed. It is hard to say which is worse because they both make it impossible to live a normal life.
Have you ever had a period of time, at least two weeks, where you didn't experience any significant depressive symptoms or psychotic symptoms, allowing you to function relatively normally?

I honestly can't recall any period like that over the last year and a half. It feels like I haven't had a single moment where I felt completely normal and free of all these symptoms. One or both of these issues have always been there, making it impossible to just function normally.

The fact that the patient cannot recall a period without either depressive or psychotic symptoms in the last year and a half further supports the idea that these symptoms are intertwined, which is characteristic of schizoaffective disorder. Thus, both diagnoses remain as candidates for now, as the interview continues to gather more specific details about the timing and dominance of symptoms.
